content: Certain medications used to treat seizures, such as carbamazepine and phenobarbital, may interact with other drugs. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms like loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call 911. If the symptoms are not life-threatening, contact a poison control center right away. In the United States, you can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition. Laboratory and medical tests, such as liver and kidney function tests or blood mineral level assessments, should be conducted before starting this medication and periodically while you are taking it. It is important to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. The information provided here is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
